content.text:
I submitted **index 16** (Sb 0.68 / Zn 0.32), which had the highest EQE of the three compositions I measured: 0.0069%. All three merit measurements are used; I used none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | Nearby known phase | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.23 | Zn7Sb2O12 (spinel) | 0.0029 |
| 16 | 0.68 | ZnSb2O6 (trirutile) | **0.0069** |
| 22 | 0.80 | ZnSb2O6 plus Sb oxides | 0.0029 |

- **Signal is weak everywhere.** All three EQEs are very low. That fits zinc–antimony oxides with band gaps of about 3.3 eV, which absorb little of the 2.7 eV illumination.
- **Band-gap predictions were wrong.** The MEGNet model predicted gaps near 2 eV for both main phases, which would absorb 2.7 eV light. The low measurements suggest those predictions were too low. That also undercut my reason for trying index 22: I expected mixed-valence Sb oxides at the Sb-rich end to absorb visible light, but they didn't.
- **Large parts of the line were never measured.** With only three measurements, the best composition in the library could lie there, for example between index 16 and index 22, or around index 13. So index 16 is only the best of what I measured.
